title: Platelet-Derived Extracellular Vesicle Functionalization of Ti Implants
protocol: Thaw PL at room temperature.
Centrifuge PL at 1,500 x g for 15 min at 4 °C.
Discard the pellet as it contains cell debris.
Collect the supernatant and perform two consecutive centrifugations at 10,000 x g for 30 min at 4 °C.
Filter the supernatant first through a 0.8 µm porous membrane.
Filter the filtered PL through a 0.2 µm porous membrane.
Pool the filtered PL and store at -20 °C until use.
Equilibrate the column coupled to chromatography equipment with filtered PBS at a flow rate of 0.5 mL/min.
Load the processed PL (5 mL) into the equipment using a syringe.
Inject the PL into the column.
Start collecting 5 mL fractions in 15 mL tubes.
Collect EVs enriched fractions and store them at -80 °C until use.
Characterize all fractions by protein quantification and immunodetection to determine the one enriched with EVs.
Wash the chromatographic column with 30 mL of 0.2% NaOH solution.
Store the column in 20% ethanol solution once it reaches equilibrium.
Dilute the EVs (1:1000) in 0.2 μm filtered PBS for NTA determination.
Load 1 ml of the diluted EVs with a syringe to the NTA equipment.
Inject the sample into the NTA equipment.
Follow the manufacturer's protocol for particle concentration and size distribution determination.
Determine the concentration using 1 µL of the EVs solution.
Measure the absorbance with a spectrophotometer at a wavelength of 280 nm.
Wash Ti implants with deionized (DI) water, and then discard the water.
Wash Ti implants with ethanol 70%, and then decant to remove the solution.
Place the implants in DI water and sonicate at 50 °C for 5 min.
Discard the water.
Incubate Ti implants in a 40% NaOH solution at 50 °C for 10 min with agitation.
Discard the solution.
Sonicate the implants in DI water at 50 °C for 5 min, and then remove the water.
Perform several washes with DI water until it reaches neutral pH.
Check pH with pH indicators.
Sonicate the implants in DI water at 50 °C for 5 minutes.
Remove the water.
Incubate Ti implants in a 50% HNO3 solution at 50 °C for 10 minutes with agitation.
Remove the solution.
Sonicate the implants in DI water at 50 °C for 5 minutes.
Remove the water.
Perform several washes with DI water until it reaches neutral pH.
Check pH with pH indicators.
Incubate Ti implants overnight at room temperature in DI water.
Dry off the implants under vacuum conditions at 40 °C for 10 minutes.
Work in a cell culture cabinet for cell functional studies.
Place the Ti implants in a 96-well plate with the machined side facing up.
Use a needle to set the implants back if they are turned upside-down.
Thaw the EVs solution and mix it with agitation using a vortex for 3 s.
Deposit the EVs on the Ti surface by placing drops of 40 µL of EVs solution onto the Ti.
Place the plates containing the Ti under vacuum conditions at 37 °C until drops are completely dry (~2 h).
Adjust the time depending on the number of implants and the water present in the vacuum chamber.
Incubate Ti surface with 200 μl of filtered PBS at 37°C.
Replace the PBS at different time points and store at -80°C.
Analyze stored PBS for particle studies by NTA according to the manufacturer's instructions.
Maintain hUC-MSC in DMEM low glucose supplemented with 20% FBS until use.
Change the medium twice per week for hUC-MSC culture.
Wash hUC-MSC cells in flasks with 5 mL of PBS twice.
Add 1 mL of trypsin solution to cover the monolayer of cells completely.
Remove the trypsin solution and place the cell culture flask at 37 °C for 2 min approximately.
View cell detachment under the microscope.
Resuspend detached hUC-MSC in DMEM low glucose with 1% EVs depleted FBS.
Bring hUC-MSC to a concentration of 50,000 cells/mL.
Seed 200 µL of the cell solution onto Ti implants.
Collect 50 µL of media after 48 h for cytotoxic determination using lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) activity kit.
